mainTopic: The מעמד readings and prayers, and the history of the families who brought the wood offering (קרבן עצים)
overview: This amud opens with the last words of an explanation from the previous amud. The גמרא then asks whether the people of the מעמד read their passage from a Torah scroll at מוסף or recited it by heart. A ברייתא shows that שחרית and מוסף were read from the scroll and only מנחה was said by heart. רבי יוסי argues only about who recites it at מנחה. Next the גמרא explains why a מוסף day cancels more of the מעמד prayers than a wood-offering day: the מוסף is דאורייתא, while the קרבן עצים is דרבנן. Several ברייתות then tell the history of the wood-offering days. When the exiles returned, certain families donated wood, and the נביאים made those days permanent. Under a wicked kingdom, brave people smuggled ביכורים and wood past enemy guards, and that is where some family nicknames come from. Finally, the גמרא asks who wrote the משנה's list of families, answers that it is רבי יוסי as reported by one of two תנאים, and begins a new question about 1 Tevet that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing words: the second reader has room to continue
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the previous explanation: the second reader has room to keep reading into the next paragraph.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he has room.
steps.whatsHappening: These words finish an explanation that began on the previous amud. The point is that the second reader has extra room, because he can continue into the next paragraph.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous discussion dealt with dividing a short passage among readers. The answer given there is that the second reader is not stuck: there is more text after him, so he can extend his reading. This line closes that point before the גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Room, extra space, slack

phrases.notes: Completes the answer from the previous page.

steps.title: The משנה: the long passage and reading in each prayer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that a long passage is read by two people at שחרית and מוסף, and at מנחה it is read by heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: A long passage is read by two people, in the morning prayer and in the additional prayer. And in the afternoon prayer they read it by heart, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה so it can discuss it. This quote sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of the מעמד read a section of מעשה בראשית each day. A long section is split between two readers. The wording is unclear: does 'at שחרית and מוסף' go with the first part (from the scroll)? Or does מוסף belong with מנחה (by heart)?

steps.title: How should the משנה be read?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether מוסף belongs with שחרית (read from the scroll) or with מנחה (read by heart).
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What is the משנה saying? Is it that at שחרית and מוסף they read from the scroll, and at מנחה they read by heart, the way one recites שמע? Or perhaps it is teaching this: at שחרית they read from the scroll, and at מוסף and מנחה they read by heart, the way one recites שמע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real question about how to divide the משנה's sentence. It offers two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option 1: שחרית and מוסף are both read from a Torah scroll, and only מנחה is by heart. Option 2: only שחרית is from the scroll, and both מוסף and מנחה are by heart. The whole question is where מוסף belongs.

Or perhaps

steps.title: A ברייתא: שחרית and מוסף from the scroll, מנחה by heart
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that at שחרית and מוסף they read from the scroll as usual, and only at מנחה one person reads it by heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: At שחרית and מוסף they enter the בית הכנסת and read the way they read all year. At מנחה, one person reads it by heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. The ברייתא supports Option 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא clearly puts מוסף together with שחרית, as a normal reading from the scroll. Only מנחה is done by heart. In this first opinion, a single person recites it at מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Synagogue
A single individual

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:

steps.title: רבי יוסי: everyone recites it together at מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי objects that one person cannot recite Torah by heart for the congregation, so everyone recites it together like שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: Can one individual read words of Torah by heart before the congregation? Rather, they all enter and read it by heart, the way one recites שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי challenges one detail of the first opinion. He disagrees about who recites at מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that one person may not recite Torah by heart on behalf of the public. So at מנחה, everyone says it together, the way each person says שמע. He does not argue about מוסף, so both opinions agree that only מנחה is by heart. That answers the question in favor of Option 1.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disputes the first opinion
But can it be? (a rhetorical challenge)
Before the congregation, on the public's behalf
Rather
All of them

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that שחרית and מוסף were read from the Torah scroll, and only מנחה was by heart. The dispute is only whether one person or everyone recites at מנחה.

steps.title: The משנה: days with הלל have no מעמד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: any day with הלל has no מעמד reading (at שחרית), and so on for days with מוסף and קרבן עצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any day that has הלל has no מעמד, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up a question about the משנה's list of days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה gives three rules. A day with הלל has no מעמד at שחרית. For the other two rules, the גמרא here follows the version that בן עזאי reports in the name of רבי יהושע: a day with a קרבן מוסף has no מעמד at מנחה, and a day with a קרבן עצים (wood offering) has none at נעילה. (רבי עקיבא's version in the משנה reverses these two.) The question that follows is about these last two rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Psalms of praise said on festive days
The group of Israelites who stood for the daily offering and read Torah

phrases.english: Any day that has הלל
has no מעמד, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues with the rules for מוסף and קרבן עצים.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הַלֵּל אֵין בּוֹ מַעֲמָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Special days cancel some of the מעמד prayers: הלל cancels שחרית, מוסף cancels מנחה, and קרבן עצים cancels נעילה.

steps.title: Why does מוסף cancel more than the wood offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference there is between a מוסף day and a קרבן עצים day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between this and that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה treats these two kinds of days differently. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוסף day cancels the מעמד from מנחה onward, but a קרבן עצים day cancels only נעילה. Both are special offerings, so why does one have a stronger effect?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
Between this and that

phrases.english: What is the difference between this and that?
phrases.notes: Between a מוסף day and a קרבן עצים day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה הֶפְרֵשׁ בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the distinction in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does a מוסף day cancel more of the מעמד than a קרבן עצים day?

steps.title: Torah law versus rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The מוסף is דאורייתא, while the קרבן עצים is דרבנן, so the מוסף has the stronger effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are words of Torah, and those are words of the scribes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is in the source of each day's status. The מוסף comes from the Torah, while the wood offering comes from the Rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A day with a Torah-required קרבן מוסף is more important, so it pushes aside more of the מעמד, starting from מנחה. The קרבן עצים is only a rabbinic institution, so it pushes aside only the last prayer, נעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah law (דאורייתא)
Rabbinic law (דרבנן)
The wood offering brought by certain families on set days

steps.whatToRemember: A Torah-level special day (מוסף) cancels more of the מעמד than a rabbinic-level one (קרבן עצים).

phrases.english: These are words of Torah,
phrases.notes: The מוסף offering.

phrases.english: and these are words of the scribes.
phrases.notes: The wood offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַלָּלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְהַלָּלוּ דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the distinction.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מוסף is required by Torah law and the קרבן עצים by rabbinic law, so the מוסף overrides more of the מעמד.

steps.title: Why did the משנה need to list the wood-offering days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase about the times for the wood offering, and a ברייתא asks why these special days had to be set at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The times of the wood of the כהנים and the people, etc.' The רבנן taught: Why did they need to set times for the wood of the כהנים and the people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה, the list of days when certain families brought wood for the מזבח. It quotes a ברייתא that asks why these days were needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has a simple basis. The בית המקדש normally bought its wood with public funds, so why would private families have their own special wood days? The ברייתא wants the history behind the custom.

keyTerms.meaning: The wood donated by priests and the people for the fire on the מזבח
'Our Rabbis taught.' This introduces a ברייתא
'They needed to say.' It asks why something had to be stated or set up
'Etc.' The quote from the משנה continues beyond what is written here

steps.title: The returning exiles found no wood, so these families donated
steps.stepSummary: When the exiles came back from בבל, there was no wood in the storage room, so these families stepped forward and donated their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: When the people of the exile came up, they did not find wood in the chamber. So these families stood up and donated wood from their own property.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a piece of history. At the start of the second בית המקדש there was no wood, and these particular families gave their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the origin of the custom. The families earned their special days because they stepped in when the בית המקדש needed them. The next step explains why the custom continued after the emergency ended.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of the exile, the Jews who returned from בבל
A chamber in the בית המקדש, here the storage room for wood
They donated voluntarily

phrases.english: They said:
When the people of the exile came up (to Jerusalem)
they did not find wood in the chamber,
and these (families) arose and donated from their own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: כְּשֶׁעָלוּ בְּנֵי הַגּוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The days started because these families donated wood when the returning exiles found the storage room empty

steps.title: The נביאים made the donation days permanent
steps.stepSummary: The נביאים of that time ruled that these families would always donate on their days, even when the storage room was full.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the prophets among them made this condition: even if the chamber is full of wood, these families will still donate from their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its answer. It explains why the custom lasted after the emergency was over: the נביאים fixed it as a permanent rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 explained only why the families donated at first. This step explains why the days stayed after wood was no longer short. The rule became a lasting honor that did not depend on need. That is why these days count as a kind of festival for those families.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a condition or stipulation
Prophets, here those of the early second בית המקדש period
Full

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the קרבן עצים days were fixed for every generation. It also explains the earlier step that called the קרבן עצים a rabbinic institution.

phrases.english: And so the prophets among them stipulated:
that even if the chamber is full of wood
these (families) will donate from their own,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The נביאים made the donation days a permanent rule, whether or not wood was needed

steps.title: A פסוק in נחמיה supports the fixed wood days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק from נחמיה about casting lots for the wood offering 'at appointed times, year by year'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And we cast lots for the wood offering, the priests, the Levites and the people, to bring it to the house of our God, by our fathers' houses, at appointed times year by year, to burn on the altar of ה׳ our God, as written in the Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to support what it just said about the permanent wood days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'appointed times, year by year' show that the wood donations were set for fixed dates every year. They were not a one-time emergency gift. The words 'by our fathers' houses' show that the days went to specific families.

keyTerms.meaning: Lots, used to assign who brings wood and when
The wood offering for the מזבח
Appointed, fixed times
To burn

steps.whatToRemember: The wood days began when the exiles returned and found no wood. The נביאים made them permanent, and the פסוק in נחמיה says 'at appointed times, year by year'.

steps.title: Who were the pestle-smugglers and the fig-pressers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה about the fifteenth of Av, and a ברייתא asks who the strangely named families were.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And with them were priests and Levites and anyone who, etc.' The רבנן taught: Who were the descendants of the pestle-smugglers and the descendants of the fig-pressers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about who brought wood on the fifteenth of Av. It asks about two families with unusual names. This sets up a story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists 'בני גונבי עלי' and 'בני קוצעי קציעות' without explaining them. These names sound like nicknames, so the ברייתא asks what they mean.

steps.title: The story begins: a wicked kingdom bans wood and ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts its answer with a story. A wicked kingdom banned bringing wood for the מזבח and ביכורים to ירושלים, and put guards on the roads.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Once the wicked kingdom made a decree of persecution against Israel, that they may not bring wood for the altar fire and may not bring first fruits to Jerusalem. They placed guards on the roads, the way ירבעם בן נבט had placed guards, so that Israel would not go up for the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins answering through a story. This step only sets the scene of the decree and the guards. The rest of the story continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree banned two things: wood for the מזבח and ביכורים. The guards made it dangerous to travel to ירושלים. The next step tells how these families smuggled ביכורים past the guards, and that trick (the pestle and the dried figs) is where their nicknames come from.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked kingdom, here understood as יון (Greece)
A decree of persecution meant to force Jews to abandon מצוות
The arranged pile of wood burning on the מזבח

steps.title: The fig-basket trick for bringing ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: Righteous people covered their ביכורים baskets with dried figs and carried a pestle. They told the guards they were going to press fig cakes, then took the ביכורים to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did the worthy, sin-fearing people of that generation do? They took baskets of ביכורים, covered them with dried figs, and carried them with a pestle on their shoulders. When they reached the guards, the guards asked, 'Where are you going?' They answered, 'To make two round cakes of pressed figs, using the mortar up ahead and the pestle on our shoulders.' Once they got past the guards, they decorated the baskets and brought them to ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story from step 14 and tells how righteous people tricked the guards so they could still bring ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dried figs on top made the baskets look like ordinary fig loads, and the pestle supported their cover story. This explains the strange family names in the משנה. They are remembered as the people who carried a pestle (עלי) and who handled cut dried figs (קציעות).

keyTerms.meaning: Baskets of first fruits brought to the בית המקדש
Dried, cut figs
A pestle, the pounding tool used with a mortar
Guards or checkpoints stationed on the roads
Round cakes of pressed figs
A mortar, the bowl for pounding

steps.confusionAlert: The people did not lie about having figs. The figs were real, but they were only a cover laid over the ביכורים hidden underneath.

phrases.english: What did the worthy and sin-fearing people do
of that generation?
They brought baskets of first fruits
and covered them with dried figs, and took them,
with a pestle on their shoulders.
And when they reached the guards,
the guards said to them: Where are you going?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרִין לָהֶם: לַעֲשׂוֹת שְׁנֵי עִגּוּלֵי דְבֵילָה
phrases.english: They said to them: To make two round cakes of pressed figs
with the mortar that is ahead of us,
and with the pestle that is on our shoulders.
As soon as they passed the guards,
they decorated the baskets,
and brought them to Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עָשׂוּ כְּשֵׁרִין וְיִרְאֵי חֵטְא שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story begun in step 14 by describing how the righteous got around the ban
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who were the families with strange names mentioned in the משנה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They were the people who smuggled ביכורים under dried figs while carrying a pestle, which is where their names come from

steps.title: Who were בני סלמאי הנתופתי?
steps.stepSummary: A תנא says that בני סלמאי הנתופתי did something similar. Another ברייתא then asks who they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Sage taught: These were the same as the sons of סלמאי הנתופתי. The Rabbis taught: Who were the sons of סלמאי הנתופתי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story to another family, בני סלמאי הנתופתי, and introduces a ברייתא that asks who they were. This is a setup line for the next story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name סלמאי is unusual, so the ברייתא asks where it comes from. The answer will tie the name to the word סולם (ladder).

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was taught', which introduces a teaching from the era of the תנאים
The descendants of סלמאי from נטופה, a family that donated wood
'The Rabbis taught', which introduces a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי סַלְמַאי הַנְּתוֹפָתִי.
phrases.english: A Sage taught: These were also the sons of Salmai of Netophat.
The Rabbis taught:
Who are the sons of Salmai of Netophat?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי סַלְמַאי הַנְּתוֹפָתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ביכורים story to a second family name and a parallel story
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the origin of the name בני סלמאי הנתופתי?

steps.title: The decree banning wood for the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that a wicked kingdom banned bringing wood for the מזבח and placed guards on the roads, just as ירבעם בן נבט had done.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Once, the wicked kingdom made a decree of persecution against the Jews, forbidding them to bring wood for the מזבח. They placed guards on the roads, the same way ירבעם בן נבט placed guards on the roads so that the Jews would not go up to ירושלים for the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins its answer by setting the scene. It describes the decree and the guards, which prepares us for the trick in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This decree sounds like the one in step 14, but it is a separate ברייתא with its own purpose: explaining the name סלמאי. Here the ban is about wood for the מערכה, the fire on the מזבח. The comparison to ירבעם בן נבט sets up the curse of the wicked at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree of religious persecution meant to force Jews to give up the Torah
The arrangement of wood burning on the מזבח
The first king of the northern kingdom, who blocked people from going to ירושלים
For the pilgrimage festival

phrases.english: They said: Once,

phrases.aramaic: גָּזְרָה מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה שְׁמָד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: the wicked kingdom issued a decree of persecution against the Jews
that they may not bring wood for the altar's arrangement,
and they placed guards on the roads

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהוֹשִׁיב יָרׇבְעָם בֶּן נְבָט עַל הַדְּרָכִים,
phrases.english: the way Jeroboam son of Nevat placed guards on the roads,
so that the Jews would not go up for the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: פַּעַם אַחַת גָּזְרָה מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about בני סלמאי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The background: a ban on bringing wood for the מזבח, enforced by guards on the roads

steps.title: The ladder trick for bringing wood
steps.stepSummary: Sin-fearing people built ladders out of their logs and claimed they were going to fetch young doves. Once past the guards, they took the ladders apart and brought the wood to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did the sin-fearing people of that generation do? They took their logs and made ladders, put them on their shoulders, and set off. When they reached the guards, the guards asked, 'Where are you going?' They answered, 'To bring young doves from the dovecote up ahead, using the ladders on our shoulders.' Once they got past the guards, they took the ladders apart and brought the wood up to ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells the clever trick that gave the family its name. The wood for the מזבח was disguised as ladders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a ladder to reach a dovecote looked normal, so the guards suspected nothing. The name סלמאי comes from סולם, the ladder that hid the wood. This mirrors the fig trick in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Their cut logs of wood
Ladders; the source of the name סלמאי
Young doves or pigeons
A dovecote, a house for doves
They took them apart

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why these families earned a permanent right to donate wood on their own days: they risked their lives to keep the מזבח going.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשׂוּ יִרְאֵי חֵטְא שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר?
phrases.english: What did the sin-fearing people of that generation do?
They brought their logs and made ladders,
and placed them on their shoulders and went on their way.
When they reached the guards,
the guards said to them: Where are you going?
They said to them: To bring young doves
from the dovecote ahead of us
with the ladders on our shoulders.
As soon as they passed the guards,
they took the ladders apart and brought them,
and took them up to Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עָשׂוּ יִרְאֵי חֵטְא שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by describing the ladder trick
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בני סלמאי are named for the ladders (סולמות) they used to smuggle wood to the מזבח

steps.title: The righteous are blessed, the wicked are forgotten
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes with a פסוק: the memory of righteous people like these families is a blessing, while the name of ירבעם בן נבט and those like him will rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: About them, and about people like them, the פסוק says: 'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing.' And about ירבעם בן נבט and his companions it says: 'But the name of the wicked shall rot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the stories with a lesson from a פסוק in משלי that contrasts the righteous with the wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both halves of one פסוק (משלי י:ז) are used here. The families who risked their lives are remembered with honor on their own wood-offering days. ירבעם, who blocked people from reaching ירושלים, is remembered only for shame.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing'
'The name of the wicked shall rot'
Others like them

steps.whatToRemember: The strange family names in the משנה honor people who outsmarted enemy guards to bring ביכורים and wood for the מזבח. Their reward was a lasting memory and a permanent day to donate wood.

phrases.english: And about them and those like them
the verse says: 'The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing',
and about Jeroboam son of Nevat and his companions
it is said: 'But the name of the wicked shall rot.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲלֵיהֶם וְעַל כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the stories with a moral lesson from a פסוק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Righteous self-sacrifice for the עבודה earns an eternal blessed memory, while those who block it are remembered in disgrace

steps.title: Who are the descendants of פחת מואב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about בני פחת מואב on the 20th of Av. It then brings a ברייתא with two opinions: רבי מאיר says they are בני דוד, and רבי יוסי says they are בני יואב בן צרויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: on the twentieth of Av, the wood was brought by the descendants of פחת מואב בן יהודה. A תנא taught: the descendants of פחת מואב בן יהודה are really the descendants of דוד בן יהודה. That is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יוסי says: they are really the descendants of יואב בן צרויה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה's list and brings a ברייתא that tells us who this family really is. The ברייתא has two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'פחת מואב' hints at a family with a link to מואב. That fits the line of רות המואביה, who is דוד's great-grandmother. רבי מאיר says the name means דוד's family. רבי יוסי says it means יואב's family, since יואב's mother צרויה was ישי's daughter and also came from רות.

keyTerms.meaning: Family name in the list; literally 'governor of מואב', hinting at a link to מואב
A teacher of ברייתא taught (introduces a ברייתא)
'They are the very same' — identifies one group with another
'The words of' — tells you whose opinion this is
דוד's general, son of דוד's sister צרויה

phrases.english: On the twentieth of it (of Av),
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה; 'בו' refers back to the month of Av.

phrases.english: the descendants of Pachat Moav ben Yehuda (brought wood).

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: בְּנֵי פַּחַת מוֹאָב בֶּן יְהוּדָה —
phrases.english: A Tanna taught: the descendants of Pachat Moav ben Yehuda —
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: they are the very same as the descendants of David ben Yehuda,
phrases.notes: דוד descends from רות the Moabite, which explains 'מואב'.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי יוֹאָב בֶּן צְרוּיָה.
phrases.english: they are the very same as the descendants of Yoav ben Tzeruya.
phrases.notes: צרויה was ישי's daughter, so she also descended from רות.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: בְּנֵי פַּחַת מוֹאָב בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the stories (steps 14-19) to the next line in the משנה's list of wood-bringing families.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: בני פחת מואב = בני דוד. רבי יוסי: בני פחת מואב = בני יואב בן צרויה.

steps.title: Who are the descendants of עדין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about בני עדין on the 20th of Elul. A ברייתא gives two views: רבי יהודה says they are בני דוד, and רבי יוסי again says they are בני יואב בן צרויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: on the twentieth of Elul, the wood was brought by the descendants of עדין בן יהודה, and so on. The רבנן taught: the descendants of עדין בן יהודה are really the descendants of דוד בן יהודה. That is רבי יהודה's view. רבי יוסי says: they are really the descendants of יואב בן צרויה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another family from the משנה's list. Another ברייתא tells us who that family really is, with two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the last step, but here the other opinion belongs to רבי יהודה, not רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה links עדין to דוד, since דוד is called 'עדינו' in שמואל ב׳ כג:ח. רבי יוסי stays consistent: for him, both פחת מואב and עדין are יואב's family.

keyTerms.meaning: Family name; understood as a name for דוד (or for יואב, according to רבי יוסי)
'Our Rabbis taught' — introduces a ברייתא
The month of Elul
'Etc.' — the rest of the quoted line

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the names. In step 20 the one who says 'בני דוד' is רבי מאיר. Here it is רבי יהודה. In both, רבי יוסי says 'בני יואב'. This matters for the question that comes next.

phrases.english: On the twentieth of Elul,
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: the descendants of Adin ben Yehuda, etc.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּנֵי עָדִין בֶּן יְהוּדָה —
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: the descendants of Adin ben Yehuda —

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: they are the very same as the descendants of David ben Yehuda,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי יוֹאָב בֶּן צְרוּיָה.
phrases.english: they are the very same as the descendants of Yoav ben Tzeruya.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּנֵי עָדִין בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel identification for the next family in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: בני עדין = בני דוד. רבי יוסי: בני עדין = בני יואב בן צרויה.

steps.title: Whose view does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on 1 Tevet, בני פרעוש 'returned a second time.' It asks who the author of the משנה is, and says it cannot be רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, or רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: on the first of Tevet, the descendants of פרעוש came back a second time, and so on. Who is the author of our משנה? It is not רבי מאיר, not רבי יהודה, and not רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of the list and asks which תנא wrote this משנה. It says none of the three fits. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה points out only one family that came twice: פרעוש. It brought wood on 5 Av and again on 1 Tevet. That suggests no other family in the list repeats. But the ברייתות we just learned make another family repeat, so the משנה's wording seems to clash with each of those תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of Tevet
They returned / came back
A second time
A family that brought wood on 5 Av and again on 1 Tevet
'Who is (the author of) our משנה?'

phrases.english: On the first of Tevet,
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: the descendants of Parosh returned a second time, etc.
phrases.notes: They had already brought wood on 5 Av.

phrases.english: Who is the author of our Mishnah?
It is not Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: and not Rabbi Yehuda, and not Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? לָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two ברייתות just quoted to test the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the משנה's list follows.

steps.title: Each תנא would make a different family repeat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the משנה fits none of them. Under רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה, בני דוד appear twice. Under רבי יוסי, בני יואב appear twice. So the משנה should have said that family 'returned a second time.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה follows רבי מאיר, it should say: the descendants of דוד בן יהודה came back a second time! If it follows רבי יהודה, it should say: the descendants of דוד בן יהודה came back a second time! If it follows רבי יוסי, it should say: the descendants of יואב בן צרויה came back a second time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through each of the three תנאים. For each one, it shows how the משנה's wording would have to be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בני דוד already appear in the list on 20 Tammuz. For רבי מאיר, פחת מואב (20 Av) is also דוד, so דוד's family comes twice. For רבי יהודה, עדין (20 Elul) is also דוד, so again דוד's family comes twice. For רבי יוסי, both פחת מואב and עדין are יואב, so יואב's family comes twice. In every case, the משנה should have used 'שבו... שניה' for that family, but it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: If
'Let it teach' — the משנה should have said
דוד's family, already listed on 20 Tammuz

steps.confusionAlert: Why would בני דוד be 'returning'? Because the משנה already lists them on 20 Tammuz. If פחת מואב or עדין is also דוד, then דוד's family shows up again later in the year.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה names only one family that came twice (פרעוש). The view that a later family is really בני דוד (רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה), or really בני יואב (רבי יוסי), would add a second repeating family. The next step answers who the משנה's author is.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Meir, let it teach:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁבוּ בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה שְׁנִיָּה!
phrases.english: 'the descendants of David ben Yehuda returned a second time'!
phrases.notes: Because for him, פחת מואב (20 Av) = דוד, who already came on 20 Tammuz.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yehuda, let it teach:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁבוּ בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה שְׁנִיָּה!
phrases.english: 'the descendants of David ben Yehuda returned a second time'!
phrases.notes: Because for him, עדין (20 Elul) = דוד.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yosei, let it teach:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁבוּ בְּנֵי יוֹאָב בֶּן צְרוּיָה שְׁנִיָּה!
phrases.english: 'the descendants of Yoav ben Tzeruya returned a second time'!
phrases.notes: Because for him, both פחת מואב and עדין = יואב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר, לִיתְנֵי: שָׁבוּ בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה שְׁנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the claim from step 22 by testing each תנא against the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה follows רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, or רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each of these views makes a second family appear twice in the list. Yet the משנה uses 'returned a second time' only for פרעוש.

steps.title: The author really is רבי יוסי, reported by two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יוסי. Two תנאים report his view differently. Each says only one family, either בני פחת מואב or בני עדין, came from יואב, so no family is listed twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה follows רבי יוסי. There are two תנאים who each report רבי יוסי's view in a different way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty from the last step. It says the משנה does follow רבי יוסי after all, but in a version of his view where no family appears twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that under רבי יוסי, בני יואב seemed to appear twice: as בני פחת מואב and as בני עדין. The answer is that the two ברייתות are really two different reports of רבי יוסי's view. One report says only בני פחת מואב are from יואב, and the other says only בני עדין are. In either version, no family brings wood twice, so the only family that 'returned a second time' is בני פרעוש, exactly as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. Used to go back to an option that was just rejected.
Two תנאים (sages of the משנה era)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי יוסי. The two ברייתות are two different reports of his view, and in each one only one family is from יואב. So only בני פרעוש come back a second time.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי himself holds both views at once. The point is that two different students reported his position in two different ways.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one Tanna's view into two separate reports (תרי תנאי אליבא דפלוני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי holds that both בני פחת מואב and בני עדין are בני יואב, so יואב's family appears twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each report of רבי יוסי links only one family to יואב, so no family repeats except בני פרעוש.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on 1 Tevet and introducing מר קשישא's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that on 1 Tevet there was no מעמד. It then introduces מר קשישא בריה דרב חסדא speaking to רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'On the first of Tevet there was no מעמד, etc.' מר קשישא, son of רב חסדא, said to רב אשי:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes a new part of the משנה and introduces a speaker whose question comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that on 1 Tevet there was no מעמד at all. That day had three extra things: a מוסף offering for ראש חודש, הלל for חנוכה, and a wood offering. The גמרא now starts a new topic by quoting this line, and מר קשישא is about to ask רב אשי about it.
